# AI Integration Requirements Checklist: AI Chat Integration

**Purpose**: Assess whether requirements for the configurable AI service, limited assistant capability, privacy boundary, and recovery behavior are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before implementation review.
**Created**: 2026-09-18
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the required operator-supplied AI service settings and their confidentiality boundaries completely defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK002 Are the compatibility criteria for alternative service locations defined beyond the phrase "same conversational request and response contract"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for configuration that is syntactically present but rejected by the selected service? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK004 Is the fixed assistant policy's required wording or equivalent acceptance standard specified sufficiently to determine whether its three obligations are retained? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK005 Are the boundaries of the initial date-time capability, including its time basis and permitted invocation conditions, fully specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK006 Does the specification define whether prior messages in the active conversation are available to the assistant for subsequent answers? [Gap, Assumptions, Key Entities]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK007 Are the generated-response requirements consistent with the retained transient-conversation assumption and any intended multi-turn context boundary? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK008 Are the service-unavailability, invalid-configuration, and unusable-response failure categories consistently distinguished between the specification and design contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009, contracts/model-service-contract.md]
- [x] CHK009 Are the confidentiality prohibitions for credentials, service addresses, user messages, and diagnostics consistent across requirements, entities, and assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-008, §FR-009, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK010 Are the restriction to one date-time capability and the expected handling of any other requested capability consistent across the scope, edge cases, and requirements? [Consistency, Edge Cases, Spec §FR-010]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK011 Can "generated assistant response" be objectively distinguished from a copied or reformatted user submission in every acceptance scenario? [Measurability, User Story 1, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002]
- [x] CHK012 Is the requirement to avoid revealing "inner workings" defined with clear inclusion and exclusion criteria for user-visible answers? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK013 Are the criteria for a "clear, retry-oriented" failure message defined sufficiently to assess consistency across all failure classes? [Clarity, User Story 3, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK014 Are the date-time accuracy and format expectations measurable for requests made near a calendar or time-zone boundary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK015 Is the expected prototype-load profile for the 100-submission, 10-second responsiveness outcome defined well enough to make results comparable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [x] CHK016 Are primary, validation, provider-failure, configuration-failure, malformed-response, and retry scenarios all specified with an unambiguous conversation-state outcome? [Coverage, User Stories 1-3, Edge Cases, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for a response that contains only whitespace, non-displayable content, or prohibited internal detail? [Coverage, Edge Cases, Spec §FR-003, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for a model request with malformed, non-empty, repeated, or unsupported date-time capability arguments? [Coverage, Edge Cases, Spec §FR-004, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK019 Does the specification define the intended recovery behavior when a retry encounters a different failure category than the original attempt? [Gap, User Story 3, Assumptions]

## Non-Functional Requirements and Dependencies

- [x] CHK020 Are the timeout, capacity, and failure-degradation expectations for the external service specified without conflicting with the 10-second user-visible responsiveness target? [Consistency, Spec §SC-002, Assumptions, plan.md §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK021 Are privacy-safe diagnostic requirements specific enough to distinguish permitted aggregate operational signals from prohibited identifiers, content, and provider metadata? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK022 Are accessible feedback requirements defined for each added or changed chat state, including unavailable service and invalid configuration? [Gap, User Story 3, Service Constraints]
- [x] CHK023 Are the assumptions about authorized service access, outbound connectivity, and provider responsibility documented as deployment dependencies with ownership and failure implications? [Dependencies, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK024 Are rollout and rollback criteria for the new external dependency traceable to the measurable success criteria and privacy requirements? [Traceability, Spec §SC-002, §SC-005, plan.md §Rollout & Rollback]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
